name: fd-timberframe-load-path
source_domain: Timber-frame carpentry by scribe rule and square rule — laying out a frame from irregular hewn stock on a layout floor, scribing each joint to its actual mating timber, dry-assembling bents flat on the ground, drawboring pegs that pull a joint permanently tight, working to a datum rather than to the adjacent piece, and the single-day raising where every accumulated misfit appears at once.
distance_rationale: Timber framing is a pre-industrial building craft with no shared vocabulary, tooling, or literature with software process design, so it imports no software habits. What it imports is a mature discipline of assembly sequencing under irreversibility: the layout floor where re-cutting is cheap, the dry fit that must assemble a whole bent before raising day, the drawbored peg that cannot be driven back out, the datum that stops error referencing itself, the member the pile simply cannot yield, and the distinction between a joint that reads tight and a joint that bears load. Every one of those is a question this goal asks — order of operations, sample size, a `success` slot the stock does not contain, DONE WHEN clauses with nothing to measure against, and the cost of a format change after pkg/tui has read it.
expected_isomorphisms: dry-assembling a whole bent flat on the ground before raising day ↔ confirming one card before phase 2 reads the format — a dry fit assembles a bent, and one card is one joint

scribe rule (each timber cut to its actual mate, non-interchangeable) versus square rule (cut to a theoretical member so any brace fits any post) ↔ a card scribed to its own repo versus one a fixed-width TUI row must render across 82 irregular projects

the member the pile cannot yield — no straight tie beam in the stock ↔ `success` drafting 0/5, which is a frame problem, not a scheduling one, and is answered by importing, leaving the bay open, or changing the frame

drawbored pegs, driven to pull a joint permanently tight and removable only by destroying it ↔ field names, per-field states, strength.score shape and card_version:1 once the ranker and the row depend on them with no migration path
plumb bob, framing square and equal diagonals as external datums ↔ DONE WHEN clauses measured against something outside themselves versus clauses that check their own output
a decorative member that carries no load and cannot be told from a structural one in a drawing ↔ a card slot that no consumer — gate, ranker, row state, funding copy — actually reads
raising day, one irreversible event with a crowd standing around ↔ the first session where the TUI renders real project rows from real cards and every accumulated misfit lands at once
focus: Assembly order, the fit between a six-field frame and the irregular stock it must be cut from, and which joints in this goal actually bear load — what can still be re-cut on the layout floor versus what is drawbored the moment the TUI reads the format.
persona: Apply the perspective of a timber framer laying out a frame from irregular hewn stock. Such a reviewer trusts nothing that has not been dry-assembled flat on the ground, measures against a datum rather than against the adjacent piece, knows a joint can read tight and carry nothing, and treats a drawbored peg as final: a mortise cut in the wrong face is a morning's work on the layout floor and a scarf repair once the frame is up.
decision_lens: Rank findings by what they cost to discover later in the assembly sequence. Anything that forces re-cutting cards or the ranker after phase 2 reads the format is P0. A DONE WHEN clause with no datum, or a joint that reads tight and bears no load, is P1. A member the stock cannot yield being scheduled as fill-later work is P1. Misfits still correctable on the layout floor are P2.
review_areas: Dry fit versus one joint: confirming unc-rancher tests one card, not the frame. State what a second, worse-stocked subject would expose that the first cannot, and what that costs.
Ranking with nothing to bear against: DONE WHEN requires ranking to match ruling 11 against real card strengths with exactly one real card. Say what that clause can actually verify.
The member the stock cannot yield: success drafted 0/5. Rule it as import, open bay (declined), or wrong frame — not as a slot to fill later once someone gets around to it.
Drawbores: name every decision this goal makes irreversible once pkg/tui reads the format — field names, states, strength.score shape, row-state count — and which can still be undone.
Datum, not eyeball: for each DONE WHEN clause name the external reference it is measured against. 'Four visibly distinct row states' — distinct to whom, checked by what?
Square-rule assumption: one TUI layout reads 82 cards scribed to their own repos. Find where per-project prose will not fit a shared row, and what gets truncated when it does not.
Load path: trace what bears weight if a card is wrong — plan gate, rank position, row state, funding copy. Name any of the six slots that no consumer reads; that member is decoration.
Raising order: ask what phase 2 forces to be final that the confirm step was meant to leave open, and whether the format finding can still change the frame once the TUI is being built.

severity_examples.scenario: The confirm step produces a format finding — a field renamed, a state added, a slot split — after pkg/tui already reads the format, so every confirmed card, the ranker, and the row states must be re-cut with card_version pinned at exactly 1 and no migration path written anywhere.
severity_examples.condition: If phase 2 begins before the confirm-step format finding is written into the brainstorm as a ruling, or if the goal is executed as one continuous stretch with no stop between confirm and build.

severity_examples.scenario: DONE WHEN's 'ranking matches ruling 11 against real card strengths' is satisfiable at N=1 by any ordering whatsoever — the clause reads tight and bears no load, so the ranker ships untested against real strength values while appearing verified.
severity_examples.condition: If exactly one card is confirmed (unc-rancher) and the other 20 project rows resolve to absent, making every ordering trivially correct.

severity_examples.scenario: `success` is treated as a slot to be filled later rather than a member the stock cannot yield, so the frame is raised with the only load-bearing timber missing and ruling 11's weakest-first ordering ranks the estate on the five inferable slots.
severity_examples.condition: If the goal reaches a confirmed card with `success` declined and no ruling is recorded on whether a declined `success` may satisfy `status: confirmed`.

success_hints: Name the exact decision that becomes a drawbored peg the moment pkg/tui reads the format, and the cheapest test that could be run before it is driven.
For each DONE WHEN clause, state the datum it is measured against — or state plainly that it has none and is checking its own output.
Phrase risks as 'this is discovered on raising day' with the re-cut named: which files, how many cards, whose afternoon.
Where a slot cannot be drafted from the stock, rule import / open bay / change the frame. Never 'fill it in later'.
anti_overlap: fd-assay-mark-integrity owns certification semantics — what a confirmed mark proves, attestation, evasion of the gate. Your subject is fit, load path and assembly order, not marks.
fd-archival-backlog-appraisal owns estate scale, coverage fractions and appraisal across 82. Touch 82 only where one shared layout must fit cards scribed to irregular repos.
fd-hci-ratification-cost owns the human minute-cost of confirming; fd-datamodel-format-durability owns card-check.py parsing bugs. Cite either only as evidence a joint bears no load.
Do not re-argue whether the estate needs cards at all on documentation-strategy grounds — attack the premise only through load path: name what would visibly fail if every card were wrong.
task_context: Review docs/proposals/2026-08-13-goal-card-loop-phase2.md before any of it runs. Is the sequencing right — confirm one card, then TUI? Is unc-rancher the right first subject? Does the six-field format survive a real human confirming it, given success drafted 0/5? Are the DONE WHEN clauses checkable, and does any encode a false assumption? What would be expensive to discover only after the TUI reads the format? Attack the premise too: is a per-project why-card the right instrument for overwhelm across 82 projects, or ceremony added to an estate that already has 2270 plans nobody reads? Material: the proposal, the brainstorm's 10 decisions and open questions, card-check.py and guard-plan-needs-card.sh under dotfiles/common/. The three Autarch depends_on docs are not in the local tree — work from the proposal's own summaries and say where that limits a claim.
